note: P4295 (Pro 27:7) — a full soul loathes honey; to a hungry soul all bitter is sweet.

dims.v: satiety — the full soul that loathes even honey
the soul so full that it loathes even honey — satiety breeding disdain for good things, unable to relish what want would make sweet
the hungry soul it is set against (266497)
set against the hungry soul that relishes even the bitter
nephesh (soul/appetite) — 'one who is FULL loathes honey'; satiety despises even the sweetest good. Abundance can dull appetite and gratitude, so that plenty loathes what want would prize.
hunger — the soul to which even the bitter is sweet
the hungry soul to which everything bitter tastes sweet — want that makes even the harsh welcome, the mirror of satiety's disdain
the sated soul it is set against (266493)
set against the full soul that loathes even honey

nephesh (soul/appetite) — 'but to one who is HUNGRY everything bitter is sweet'; want transforms the bitter into the sweet. Hunger prizes what plenty scorns — a parable of how need reshapes desire and gratitude.
